name: LLM forecasting agents (direct retrieval-and-reason forecasters trading the gap)
one_line: An LLM pipeline retrieves news and data, produces a calibrated probability per market and trades the gap to the Polymarket price under deterministic risk limits.
scope: The baseline every speculative multi-agent idea must beat. Cover: state of the art vs market price (ForecastBench, Metaculus AI tournaments, Prophet Arena, live Kalshi / Polymarket LLM trading arenas: mostly negative after costs), open-source Polymarket agents and commercial 'AI quant' products, viral PnL claims and why they are unverified, where LLMs plausibly have edge (long-tail illiquid markets, breadth, rules reading, multilingual sources, speed of text digestion), design choices that matter (retrieval, ensembling, market-price anchoring, extremising, fine-tuning / RL on resolved questions), traps (backtest leakage, knowledge-cutoff contamination, Brier vs PnL, fees and spread), cost per forecast, and a deterministic sizing / risk layer. Primary source: evidence pack E7. Mine S1-discovery-candidates.json for merged_from names. Boundary: simulation / debate / internal-market / self-improving variants live in the speculative band (files 50+): reference, do not repeat.
merged_from: academic: LLM/ML forecaster with proper-scoring-rule sizing

raw_discovery_candidates.name: LLM-agent forecasting / 'AI quant' bots
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Autonomous agents that research markets and trade on their own probability estimates - heavily hyped, thinly evidenced.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Typical build: agents pull news/polls/forecasts, an LLM (or ensemble of personas) outputs a probability, and the bot trades when it differs from price. Viral claims ('4 agents on a $400 laptop, $150 -> $38,700, 91% win'; 'Claude bot turned $1 into $3.3M') are unverified, and the latter account (sovereign2013) is, per the same article, a rapid sports-arbitrage bot - its $3.59M on $402M volume is market-making-like, not LLM forecasting. A practitioner with audited numbers calls X bot posts 'absolute LARPs'. Benchmarks: only two models achieved positive returns on 38,666 markets; ten LLM agents have the forecasting power of ~1.4 independent ones (error correlation 0.70); detecting a 2% edge needs ~350 resolved predictions.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Hoped-for: cheaper breadth of research than humans. Demonstrated: mainly as coding assistant and analyst-assist, not as autonomous alpha.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: Possibly in the long tail of low-attention markets where any structured base-rate work beats vibes; unproven.
raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Correlated model errors, stale-knowledge leakage in backtests, execution costs, a reviewer's 'AI ensemble bot' lost 43.3%; scams use the 'Claude bot' narrative as bait.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Pre-register 350+ small forward predictions in fee-free geopolitics/long-tail markets and compare Brier and PnL vs market mid before allocating capital.
raw_discovery_candidates.flags: The 'AI bot' narrative is the main lure of drainer scams.
raw_discovery_candidates.adjacent_grounding: LLM forecasting benchmarks on live Polymarket data (arXiv 2604.14199 PolyBench; 2606.26583 monoculture; 2605.00420 Foresight Arena) - all listed at https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:polymarket&sortBy=submittedDate&sortOrder=descending&max_results=60

evidence.title: arXiv 2604.14199 PolyBench; 2606.26583 Preference Optimization Drives Monoculture; 2605.00420 Foresight Arena
evidence.supports: Only two models positive over 36,165 predictions; rho=0.70 -> ~1.4 effective forecasters; ~350 predictions needed to detect a 2% edge at 80% power

evidence.title: Finbold: Claude AI powered trading bot turns $1 into $3.3M (sovereign2013)
evidence.supports: The viral 'AI bot' account is described as rapid sports arbitrage; no verification of any LLM role

evidence.title: kacho.io real numbers post
evidence.supports: 'All "I built a Polymarket trading bot" posts I've read on X are absolute LARPs'; AI used to write the bot, not to predict

evidence.title: Reddit r/PillarLab 1rpul61 seven-bot review
evidence.supports: AI ensemble bot -43.3%, copy bot -23%, MM bot -52.5%, a GitHub bot was a wallet drainer

raw_discovery_candidates.name: LLM/ML forecaster with proper-scoring-rule sizing and a deterministic risk layer
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Forecast with an LLM or fine-tuned model, but size with the proper-betting rule or quarter-Kelly after a selection filter - naive edge-proportional/Kelly sizing turns a slightly-better forecaster into a loser.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: Generate probabilities p, compare with market q, and stake s = grad G(p) - grad G(q) (for Brier: 2(p-q)) rather than Kelly, which assumes p is truth. Alternatively filter candidates first (edge threshold, time-normalised return, per-event caps, drawdown halts enforced outside the prompt) and then apply quarter-Kelly. Expected profit decomposes into score gap + Bregman divergence - liquidity loss, so the agent only trades where forecast skill beats book cost. Small, many, short-dated bets are needed for statistical power.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Marginal forecasting skill in markets where the crowd is thin or slow, converted efficiently into PnL.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: Evidence says the belief-to-trade layer, not the forecaster, separates winners from losers among otherwise identical agents.

evidence.title: When do prophets profit in prediction markets? (Gu, Kagan, Sun, Wu, Xu), arXiv
evidence.supports: Live Kalshi deployment Apr-May 2026: $200 -> $360.67 in 26 days (+80.33%, Sharpe 3.35), 129 markets, 236 orders, win rate 50.9%, fees $26.31, Gemini 3 forecaster; nearly all gain from predictive accuracy; Kelly shown to lose when the forecast is not the truth.

evidence.title: Beyond Forecasting: The Belief-to-Trade Layer in Prediction-Market Agents (Wang et al.), arXiv
evidence.supports: Same forecasts, 5 policies on 44-58 archived Polymarket trades: flat stake -10.7%, edge-proportional -55.5%, edge-filter -9.3%, risk module flat -4.7%, risk module + quarter-Kelly +15.9% (bootstrap CI +3.8%..+30.0%). Tiny sample.

evidence.title: Prediction Arena: Benchmarking AI Models on Real-World Prediction Markets (Zhang et al.), arXiv
evidence.supports: Real money, $10k per model, 57 days: Kalshi returns -16.0% to -30.8% for six frontier models; Polymarket -0.09% to -2.68%; research token volume uncorrelated with performance; one model made 664 trades at 28.8% settlement accuracy.

evidence.title: PolyBench (Cheng et al.), arXiv
evidence.supports: 38,666 markets, 7 models: only 2 profitable (+17.6%, +6.2%), five lost 9-25%; the best model's alpha disappeared above ~$500 allocations due to book slippage; rigid 0.8-0.9 confidence regardless of domain.

evidence.title: Outcome-based Reinforcement Learning to Predict the Future (Turtel et al.), arXiv
evidence.supports: 14B RL-tuned model: Brier 0.190 vs o1 0.202 but market 0.151; simulated one-share bets on 1,265 questions earn ~10% ROI (~20% on 40-60% markets) with a 1c cost - simulation, authors disclaim real-world inference.

evidence.title: arXiv listing: Foresight Arena (2605.00420); Preference Optimization Drives Monoculture in LLM Prediction Markets (2606.26583)
evidence.supports: Detecting a 2% edge at 80% power needs ~350 predictions, 1% needs ~4x more; DPO-tuned LLM agents' errors correlate at rho=0.70, so 10 agents ~ 1.4 independent forecasters - ensembles of similar LLMs add little.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Market Brier still beats the best models; capacity ~hundreds of dollars per market; LLM herd correlation means crowded identical bets; benchmark contamination; weather category was a consistent loser.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Pre-register 400 small bets with frozen prompts; evaluate score gap vs market, then PnL under proper-betting vs quarter-Kelly vs flat; stop if score gap <= 0 after 200.
raw_discovery_candidates.adjacent_grounding: Proper scoring rules / Bregman-divergence market makers (Hanson, Abernethy-Chen-Vaughan) reused as a bettor's sizing rule.

raw_discovery_candidates.name: Model-ensemble news/social probability bots (LLM or ML forecasters)
raw_discovery_candidates.one_line: Estimate probabilities from news and social data and trade divergences from the market.
raw_discovery_candidates.mechanism: An ensemble of models ingests news and social feeds, outputs probabilities per market and trades when the gap to price exceeds a threshold, retraining continuously. One widely reported wallet is said to have made $2.2M in two months this way. Controlled evaluations point the other way: frontier LLMs given real money lost on both venues, and only a minority of models are profitable in live benchmarks.
raw_discovery_candidates.edge_source: Faster or broader information aggregation than human traders.
raw_discovery_candidates.why_might_beat_market: Evidence is weak. The positive case is a single secondary report; every controlled test found in this session is negative or marginal. Treat headlines like '$1 into $3.3M' as marketing.

evidence.title: Arbitrage Bots Dominate Polymarket (BeInCrypto via Yahoo)
evidence.supports: Bot profiled by Igor Mikerin: ensemble probability models on news and social data, '$2.2 million in just two months'. Secondary report, unverified.

evidence.title: arXiv listing: Prediction Arena (2604.07355), PolyBench (2604.14199), LiveTradeBench (2511.03628)
evidence.supports: Six frontier models with $10,000 each over 57 days on Kalshi and Polymarket returned -30.8% to -1.1%; only 2 of 7 LLMs had positive returns in PolyBench; benchmark scores do not predict live trading success.

evidence.title: We lost $270 building a Polymarket trading bot
evidence.supports: ML gate 57% in training, 48-50% live; simulated +0.8% to +11.9% ROI versus real -27%; slippage and stop-loss overshoot dominate.

evidence.title: Claude AI powered trading bot turns $1 into $3.3M on Polymarket (Finbold) - HN listing, not opened
evidence.supports: Example of the hype genre; no verification.

raw_discovery_candidates.failure_modes: Correlated model errors (DPO-tuned agents collapse to ~1.4 independent forecasters per arXiv 2606.26583 listing); training-data leakage in backtests; taker fees; simulation-reality gap.
raw_discovery_candidates.cheap_validation: Forward-test only: commit forecasts on 350+ markets before resolution (the sample size one paper says is needed to detect a 2% edge) before risking capital.
